clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her early 30s presented with severe headache, bilateral tinnitus, blurry vision, nausea, anorexia, and left-sided sensory disturbances with urinary and bowel symptoms, starting 1 week prior, following a COVID-19 infection 2 weeks earlier. Neurological exam showed brisk reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, and a sensory deficit at T5-T6 on the left side. Brain and spinal MRI revealed partial thrombosis in the left transverse sinus and no spinal cord lesions. CSF analysis was normal. Treatment included anticoagulation and intravenous dexamethasone. Repeat MRI after 1 week demonstrated stable brain findings and normal spinal cord. The patient reported significant symptomatic improvement under therapy.
